bullets.title: Fed's Kashkari calls for gradual rate hikes; markets split on September move
bullets.body: Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari said 'it's time to start slowly moving interest rates up' to achieve 2% inflation, explicitly not calling for a dramatic increase and adding he wants data before September. Markets are nearly evenly split (49% hold / 47% +25bp per Kalshi), with BofA forecasting three hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec) while JPM, Goldman, and Morgan Stanley expect hold in September.

bullets.title: ADP July payrolls badly miss (+44K vs +65K est); services PMIs beat decisively
bullets.body: ADP private payrolls came in at 44K in July vs. 65K consensus and 95K prior—the weakest print in six months—with healthcare driving almost all gains and goods-producing industries posting net losses. Separately, S&P Global Services PMI surged to 54.6 (vs. 53.6 est) and the Composite hit 54.5, while ISM Services slightly missed at 54.1 vs. 54.5 est, though prices paid ran hot at 70.3 and employment was soft at 47.4.

bullets.title: S&P 500 at 7,785 (+0.63% open), hits 25th ATH of year; BofA flags 7,741 target reached, upside to 8,541
bullets.body: The S&P 500 crossed 7,700 for the first time (8th 100-pt milestone of 2026, +22% YoY) and closed at an ATH for the 25th time this year. BofA says the index has reached its 2026 target of 7,741, with technicals pointing to potential extension toward 8,000–8,541 and 7,500 as key support; they flag seasonally weak Aug–Oct as a risk. Michael Burry simultaneously warned of a potential 1987-style top.

bullets.title: Nasdaq posted 4 straight 1%-plus up days—only 18th time in index history
bullets.body: The Nasdaq 100 rallied more than 1% for four consecutive sessions, an extreme rarity occurring just 18 times since the early 1970s. SPY/QQQ/DIA call skews reached the 98th percentile, and record call volumes were flagged as potential gamma squeeze fuel, though one technician cautioned that a one-day squeeze is not a trend.

bullets.title: AI equity funds slammed in July despite strong YTD; Citadel +5.9% via Situational Awareness buyout
bullets.body: AI-focused equity funds suffered outsized July losses (Whale Rock flagship -21.7%, Long Only -18.8%), though both remain well ahead of the S&P 500 YTD (+35.1% and +36.8%). Citadel's flagship gained 5.9% in July (12% YTD) after purchasing Situational Awareness's stock portfolio at a discount, while Pershing Square gained 3.9% in July but is still -9.2% YTD.

bullets.title: GOOGL drops 4–5% on DeepMind leadership shakeup; Jeff Dean leaving to start own AI company
bullets.body: Alphabet shares fell more than 5% (~$200B market cap loss) after Google announced Demis Hassabis is stepping down as DeepMind CEO to become Chairman/Alphabet Chief Scientist, with Koray Kavukcuoglu taking over day-to-day responsibilities. Google's Chief AI Scientist Jeff Dean simultaneously departed after 27 years to start his own AI company, amplifying talent-flight concerns.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz deal in progress: draft agreed, awaits Iran Supreme Leader; US removes some Iran sanctions
bullets.body: Iranian and Omani negotiators finalized a draft agreement proposing toll-free Hormuz transit (ships enter Iran-side, exit Oman-side) valid for 2–4 months, pending final approval from Iran's Supreme Leader. The US separately removed Iran-related sanctions per Treasury, and Trump said talks are 'very good' with a deal possible 'as soon as today'; a Gulf official put odds at 50-50 by Friday. Houthi escalation (fourth maritime incident in 24 hrs off Aden, Yemen shipping routes declared unsafe) added cross-current risk.

bullets.title: Gold hits $4,238 (+4%), silver +5%, copper tops $14,000 all-time high on Hormuz optimism and supply squeeze
bullets.body: Spot gold extended gains to nearly $4,238/oz (+4%) and silver rose 5% to $62.53/oz as Hormuz deal hopes boosted rate-cut expectations. Copper topped $14,000/ton, driven by US pre-tariff stockpiling that is draining global supply ahead of potential Trump tariffs; precious metals miner AEM rallied 9%.

bullets.title: US crude inventories surprise with +2.5M bbl build vs. -1.5M expected; SPR at 35-year low
bullets.body: EIA data showed crude inventories rose 2.479M barrels (vs. consensus -1.4M draw and prior -7.2M draw) with Cushing also building +2.36M barrels, pressuring oil prices. However, distillates fell 3.5M barrels and gasoline 1.6M barrels; the Strategic Petroleum Reserve hit 305M barrels, its lowest level since February 1983. Brent crude traded near $79–$80/bbl, whipsawed by Hormuz optimism vs. Houthi escalation.

bullets.title: US Treasury holds auction sizes steady; $125B quarterly refunding raises $28.7B in new cash
bullets.body: The Treasury announced it will maintain nominal coupon, floating rate note, and TIPS auction sizes unchanged for 'at least several quarters,' with $125B in quarterly refunding and $28.7B in new cash raised. No surprises in the quarterly refunding schedule per market commentary.

bullets.title: BCA Research warns of tech-heavy household wealth concentration and potential rotation risk
bullets.body: BCA Research's MacroQuant model flagged that US household equity wealth is heavily concentrated in tech, raising potential sector rotation and recession risk if that trade unwinds.

bullets.title: BTIG echoes dot-com bubble warning; multistrat funds criticized as disguised momentum traders
bullets.body: BTIG strategists see 'echoes from dot-com' in current valuations and warn investors 'don't get burned twice.' Separately, critics argued multistrat funds marketed as 'factor-neutral' are actually high-fee momentum traders using accounting adjustments, with AI equity fund July losses exposing concentration risk.

bullets.title: Samsung and SK Hynix test Chinese chipmaking tools to hedge US export-control risk
bullets.body: Per Reuters, Samsung and SK Hynix are evaluating Chinese semiconductor equipment (including AMEC tools) for China-based fabs, incentivized by US export restrictions to diversify their supply chains away from American equipment vendors—a potential demand headwind for US chipmaking equipment suppliers.

bullets.title: Trump export controls backfiring: Korean chipmakers pivoting to Chinese equipment
bullets.body: US export controls may be accelerating Samsung and SK Hynix's evaluation of Chinese alternatives, reducing addressable market for US semiconductor equipment companies and potentially strengthening the Chinese equipment ecosystem at the expense of US suppliers.

bullets.title: NVDA up 4.3% to 2-month highs; ~$100M in bearish options flow despite rally
bullets.body: NVIDIA shares hit their highest level in over two months, rising 4.3%, buoyed by strong AI spending confidence and ANET's blowout earnings read-through. However, approximately $100M in bearish options flow was recorded today against the move, suggesting hedging or near-term directional skepticism among options traders.

bullets.title: US drafts ban on Chinese data-center optical transceivers; domestic suppliers key beneficiaries
bullets.body: The US government is reportedly drafting a ban on Chinese data-center optical transceiver imports, which could drive material supply chain redistribution. LITE, COHR, and AAOI are positioned as primary domestic beneficiaries; NVDA secured $2B capacity commitments in each of COHR and LITE to lock in supply.

bullets.title: Mortgage rates hit one-year high; lumber at 4-year highs despite housing slowdown
bullets.body: US mortgage rates reached their highest level in a year, compounding existing housing affordability pressure (Redfin estimates $70,693 income needed for a typical starter home). Paradoxically, lumber prices rose to four-year highs despite slumping home sales and declining renovation spending.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler $3T in off-balance-sheet obligations flagged; spot GPU rental rates 2x contract rates
bullets.body: A CNBC segment highlighted roughly $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations across hyperscalers, raising questions about AI capex sustainability. Separately, spot GPU rental rates are running 2x multi-year contracted rates, creating repricing risk for cloud providers as long-term deals roll off.

bullets.title: US economy in 74-month expansion—above average but short of the 128-month record
bullets.body: The US expansion has now run 74 months, above the 67-month post-WWII average but well below the record 128-month cycle. Tom Lee noted earnings growth has outpaced stock prices, suggesting relative valuation remains constructive despite all-time highs.

bullets.title: Starlink mobile creates competitive headwind for US telecoms; Bernstein says 'jab, not knockout'
bullets.body: US telecom stocks fell on Starlink mobile launch competitive concerns. Bernstein characterized the threat as a near-term tactical headwind rather than an existential threat to traditional carriers.
